lessons.title: What is dollar-cost averaging?
lessons.body: DCA means investing a fixed amount on a regular schedule. It changes timing, not market risk.

lessons.title: How Bitcoin DCA works
lessons.body: Set an amount and schedule. Each payment buys more bitcoin at lower prices and less at higher prices.

lessons.title: Why people use DCA
lessons.body: A schedule reduces timing decisions, but you keep buying during downturns.

lessons.title: DCA versus a lump sum
lessons.body: DCA spreads purchases over time; a lump sum invests at once. Results depend on timing and market conditions.

lessons.title: Understanding Bitcoin volatility
lessons.body: Bitcoin prices can rise or fall sharply, and portfolios can lose substantial value.

lessons.title: Risks and limitations
lessons.body: DCA does not guarantee returns. Fees, taxes, and custody errors affect results; don't invest essential funds.

lessons.title: Budgeting recurring purchases
lessons.body: Consider essential costs, savings, debts, and local rules before setting a recurring amount.

lessons.title: Bitcoin accumulation and self-custody
lessons.body: Self-custody gives you control of bitcoin and responsibility for key backups.

lessons.title: Transaction fees
lessons.body: Fees reduce the bitcoin received or increase its cost basis. Frequent small purchases can make fixed fees significant.

lessons.title: Reviewing a plan
lessons.body: Review plans against your budget, not recent prices. Historical results don't predict future performance.
